#!/bin/bash

# inside a quoted context. See kubernetes_jq_query for the rationale.
KIND=pods
CUSTOM_COLUMNS='NAME:.metadata.name,PHASE:.status.phase,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount,NODE:.spec.nodeName,START:.status.startTime'

SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
FILTER_PATTERN=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""
[ "$FILTER_PATTERN" = "None" ] && FILTER_PATTERN=""

# kubectl ignores -n for cluster-scoped kinds; say so instead of reporting a namespace that wasn't applied
NOTES='[]'
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
  is_kind() { awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind || index($1, kind ".") == 1 {found = 1} END {exit !found}'; }
  if kubectl api-resources --namespaced=false -o name 2>/dev/null | is_kind \
    && ! kubectl api-resources --namespaced=true -o name 2>/dev/null | is_kind; then
    NOTES=$(jq -nc --arg note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${KIND} is cluster-scoped." '[$note]')
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
fi

SCOPE_ARGS=()
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(-n "$SEL_NAMESPACE")
else
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--all-namespaces)
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(-l "$SEL_LABELS")
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--field-selector "$SEL_FIELDS")
fi

err_file=$(mktemp)
output=$(kubectl get "$KIND" "${SCOPE_ARGS[@]}" -o custom-columns="$CUSTOM_COLUMNS" 2>"$err_file")
kubectl_exit=$?
err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

SCOPE='null'
if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
    '{namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
      label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
      field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')
fi

    jq -n --arg stderr "$err_content" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
      '{count: 0, header: null, rows: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  else
    echo "=== STDERR ==="
    echo "$err_content"
    echo "=== ROWS ==="
    echo "=== COUNT ==="
    echo 0
  fi
  exit 0
fi

# Split header and data rows
header=$(echo "$output" | head -1)
if [ -n "$FILTER_PATTERN" ]; then
  data=$(echo "$output" | tail -n +2 | grep -E -- "$FILTER_PATTERN" || true)
else
  data=$(echo "$output" | tail -n +2)
fi

if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then
    count=$(echo "$data" | wc -l)
  else
    count=0
  fi

    --argjson count "$count" \
    --arg header "$header" \
    --arg stderr "$err_content" \
    --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
    '{count: $count, header: $header, rows: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
else

  echo "$err_content"
  echo "=== HEADER ==="
  echo "$header"
  echo "=== ROWS ==="
  echo "$data"
  echo "=== COUNT ==="
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then echo "$data" | wc -l; else echo 0; fi
fi

#!/bin/bash

# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables in an unquoted
# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=events
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | {type: .type, reason: .reason, object: .involvedObject.name, count: .count, last: .lastTimestamp, msg: .message}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)
# `kubectl api-resources` sorts by group name, so a CRD reusing a built-in
# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).
if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -c .)" -gt 1 ] && [[ "$API_INFO" != *" v1 "* ]]; then
  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Build API path: namespaced kinds can be listed within one namespace;
# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)
if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else
  if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

#!/bin/bash

#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps

# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=services

SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'

[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, clusterIP: .spec.clusterIP, ports: .spec.ports, selector: .spec.selector}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints

  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).

  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then

  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else

    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0

  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

#!/bin/bash

# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables in an unquoted
# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=pods
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | {ns: .metadata.namespace, name: .metadata.name, phase: .status.phase, node: .spec.nodeName, start: .status.startTime, restarts: [.status.containerStatuses[]?.restartCount], cpu: [.spec.containers[] | {n: .name, lim: .resources.limits.cpu, req: .resources.requests.cpu}]}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)
# `kubectl api-resources` sorts by group name, so a CRD reusing a built-in
# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).
if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -c .)" -gt 1 ] && [[ "$API_INFO" != *" v1 "* ]]; then
  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Build API path: namespaced kinds can be listed within one namespace;
# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)
if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else
  if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

#!/bin/bash

# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables in an unquoted
# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=endpoints
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, subsets: .subsets, endpoints: [.endpoints[]? | {ip: .addresses, ports: .ports, ready: .conditions}]}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)
# `kubectl api-resources` sorts by group name, so a CRD reusing a built-in
# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).
if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -c .)" -gt 1 ] && [[ "$API_INFO" != *" v1 "* ]]; then
  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Build API path: namespaced kinds can be listed within one namespace;
# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)
if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else
  if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.

# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='[.items[] | {kind: "deployment", name: .metadata.name, edits: [.metadata.managedFields[] | select(.manager!="kube-controller-manager") | {manager, time, hasSelector: (.fieldsV1["f:spec"]["f:selector"] != null), hasTemplate: (.fieldsV1["f:spec"]["f:template"] != null), fields: (.fieldsV1["f:spec"] | keys?)}]}]'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')

# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).

  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."

  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Build API path: namespaced kinds can be listed within one namespace;
# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)
if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else
  if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables (unquoted slot),
# then reference them only as "$VAR" - never interpolate 
# inside a quoted context. See kubernetes_jq_query for the rationale.
KIND=namespaces
CUSTOM_COLUMNS=NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.phase
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
FILTER_PATTERN=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""
[ "$FILTER_PATTERN" = "None" ] && FILTER_PATTERN=""

# kubectl ignores -n for cluster-scoped kinds; say so instead of reporting a namespace that wasn't applied
NOTES='[]'
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
  is_kind() { awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind || index($1, kind ".") == 1 {found = 1} END {exit !found}'; }
  if kubectl api-resources --namespaced=false -o name 2>/dev/null | is_kind \
    && ! kubectl api-resources --namespaced=true -o name 2>/dev/null | is_kind; then
    NOTES=$(jq -nc --arg note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${KIND} is cluster-scoped." '[$note]')
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
fi

SCOPE_ARGS=()
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(-n "$SEL_NAMESPACE")
else
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--all-namespaces)
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(-l "$SEL_LABELS")
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--field-selector "$SEL_FIELDS")
fi

err_file=$(mktemp)
output=$(kubectl get "$KIND" "${SCOPE_ARGS[@]}" -o custom-columns="$CUSTOM_COLUMNS" 2>"$err_file")
kubectl_exit=$?
err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

SCOPE='null'
if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
    '{namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
      label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
      field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')
fi

if [ $kubectl_exit -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$output" ]; then
  if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
    jq -n --arg stderr "$err_content" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
      '{count: 0, header: null, rows: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  else
    echo "=== STDERR ==="
    echo "$err_content"
    echo "=== ROWS ==="
    echo "=== COUNT ==="
    echo 0
  fi
  exit 0
fi

# Split header and data rows
header=$(echo "$output" | head -1)
if [ -n "$FILTER_PATTERN" ]; then
  data=$(echo "$output" | tail -n +2 | grep -E -- "$FILTER_PATTERN" || true)
else
  data=$(echo "$output" | tail -n +2)
fi

if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then
    count=$(echo "$data" | wc -l)
  else
    count=0
  fi
  # Rows go through stdin, not --argjson, so large tables don't hit "Argument list too long"
  printf '%s' "$data" | jq -R . | jq -s \
    --argjson count "$count" \
    --arg header "$header" \
    --arg stderr "$err_content" \
    --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
    '{count: $count, header: $header, rows: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
else
  echo "=== STDERR ==="
  echo "$err_content"
  echo "=== HEADER ==="
  echo "$header"
  echo "=== ROWS ==="
  echo "$data"
  echo "=== COUNT ==="
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then echo "$data" | wc -l; else echo 0; fi
fi

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)
# `kubectl api-resources` sorts by group name, so a CRD reusing a built-in
# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).
if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -c .)" -gt 1 ] && [[ "$API_INFO" != *" v1 "* ]]; then
  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Build API path: namespaced kinds can be listed within one namespace;
# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)
if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else
  if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

## 结论（TL;DR）

Pod 全绿是真的（12 个 Pod 全 Running/Ready、0 重启、Endpoints 都正常），但**问题不在 Pod 状态，而在两处调用链**：

1. **当前仍在持续的变慢**：`recommendationservice` 的 `ListRecommendations` 往返稳定多出 **~1.5 s**。凡是走推荐页的入口（`/product/*`、`/cart`、`/cart/checkout` 下单页）都是 **~2.1–3.1 s**，而完全不调推荐的首页 `/` 仍是 **0.29–0.35 s**。这就是"页面明显变慢但没有报错"。
2. **刚发生、已被临时绕过的一段真实故障（13:18–13:23）**：`cartservice` → `redis-cart` 连不上，前端每秒 1 条 `request error`，负载发生器累计 **14.3% 请求失败**、最大 **19.5 s**。13:23:07 `redis-cart` Service 的 `spec.selector` 被人 `kubectl patch` 后，购物车报错才停止。

---

## 证据

### 1. 慢的那一段 = recommendationservice（已确认到跳）

时间戳对齐（均取自 13:25:28–13:25:45 同一窗口）：

| 前端请求 | 请求开始 | recs 打印 `[Recv ListRecommendations]` | 广告服务收到 ad 请求 | 页面返回 | 耗时 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET /product/1YMWWN1N4O | 32.865 | 33.473（+0.61s） | 35.000 | 35.001 | 2136 ms |
| GET /product/OLJCESPC7Z | 33.815 | 34.433（+0.62s） | 35.945 | 35.946 | 2131 ms |
| GET /product/L9ECAV7KIM | 36.485 | 37.142（+0.66s） | 38.638 | 38.639 | 2182 ms |
| GET /cart | 31.651 | 31.931（+0.28s） | — | 33.819 | 2168 ms |
| GET / | 37.125 | （不调用） | — | 37.465 | 339 ms |

- 推荐服务**处理本身很快**（日志在收到调用后 30–40 ms 就打出来了，说明它内部的 productcatalog 调用已完成），但**前端要到它打印后约 1.5 s 才拿到响应**，紧接着 1–2 ms 内就发出 ad 请求、立刻返回。也就是说这 1.5 s 全部落在 recs 的响应环节。
- 反证：`adservice` 收单到页面完成只差 1–2 ms；`POST /cart`（同样是 cartservice gRPC）只要 **293–322 ms**；productcatalog/currency 在首页 0.3 s 内被调用 10 次都没问题。
- 推荐服务这段时间确有异常：`recommendationservice-6c88b5fb59-xksjg` 在 **13:20:15–13:20:22** 连续报
  `failed to connect to all addresses; ... ipv4:10.96.32.253:3550: Connection refused`（productcatalogservice 的 ClusterIP），与 `productcatalogservice` 在 **13:18:28** 被 `kubectl rollout restart`（新 ReplicaSet `productcatalogservice-9c56d9b77`，Pod 重启于 13:18:28）吻合——它的长连接被打断后，响应侧就一直卡着 1.5 s。
- 极少数请求仍是健康值（例：13:23:10 有一单 `/product` 只用 **8.7 ms**），说明是"偶发进入快路径"，典型的资源/阻塞型抖动，而不是代码级固定延迟。

### 2. 购物车那段故障（13:18–13:23，现已停止）

- `cartservice` 日志：`Can't access cart storage. StackExchange.Redis.RedisConnectionException: The message timed out in the backlog ... (5000ms) ... SocketClosed (ReadEndOfStream, last-recv: 0) on redis-cart:6379` → 之后变成 `It was not possible to connect to the redis server(s). ConnectTimeout`。
- 前端（`frontend-fd686dbb-4l28p`）同一时段每秒一条：`could not retrieve cart` / `failed to add to cart`，最后一条 **13:23:08.500**，之后到 13:26 没有再出现。
- `redis-cart` Pod 在 **13:21:57** 被重建（新 ReplicaSet `redis-cart-59d89bbbf`，revision 5，`kubectl-rollout` 修改了 template），使用 `emptyDir` → **购物车数据被清空**；重建瞬间旧连接被 `ReadEndOfStream` 掐断，而新 Pod 起来后 `cartservice` 的连接池仍在 `ws: Initializing / ConnectTimeout`。
- **13:23:07** `redis-cart` Service 的 `spec.selector` 被 `kubectl-patch` 单独接管（managed-fields 里 `f:selector` 只剩 kubectl-patch 这一条），报错正好在此刻停止 —— 这就是那句"没有报错"的原因：报错窗口是 13:18–13:23，用户看到的是残留的慢。

### 3. 负载发生器视角（`loadgenerator-6cc58494f4-nb5k7`）

```
Aggregated        5791  828(14.30%) | Avg 879ms | Max 19556ms | Med 290ms
GET  /cart         829   98(11.82%) | Avg 880   | Max 19478
POST /cart/checkout 247   48(19.43%)| Avg 1010  | Max 18597
GET  /product/*    340-376 44-61     | Avg ~900  | Med 290
GET  /             275   32(11.64%) | Avg 411   | Max 5945
```
中位数 290 ms 说明历史上大部分请求是好的，均值被这段故障期间 5–19 s 的失败请求拉高。

---

## 影响面

- **受影响（有自身报错/超时证据）**
  - `cartservice-896c89968-dxpwj`：`RedisConnectionException` / 5000 ms backlog timeout / `ConnectTimeout`（至 13:23:08）。
  - `frontend-fd686dbb-4l28p`：`severity:"error" request error`（could not retrieve cart / failed to add to cart），每秒 1 条，13:22:37–13:23:08。
  - `loadgenerator`：14.3% 请求失败，checkout 失败率 19.4%。
  - `recommendationservice-6c88b5fb59-xksjg`：13:20:15–13:20:22 `UNAVAILABLE ... Connection refused`；当前每请求 ~1.5 s 响应延迟（用户可感知的"变慢"来源）。
- **已检查、健康**：`adservice`（收单即返回）、`currencyservice`、`productcatalogservice`（首页路径 0.3 s 内多次调用正常）、`shippingservice` 无报错；12 个 Pod 全部 Ready、0 重启；所有 Service Endpoints / EndpointSlice 都指向正确且 ready 的 Pod。
- **窗口内被重建、但不是"故障"本身**：`productcatalogservice`（13:18:28 `kubectl rollout restart`）、`redis-cart`（13:21:57 `kubectl rollout restart`）、`checkoutservice`（13:21:48 `kubectl-set` 改 template）——都是人/工具主动改动，不是被驱逐（无 Evicted/OOMKilled 事件，Pod 均 restartCount=0）。
- **未检查**：节点级 CPU/Disk 压力与 NetworkPolicy（当前账号无 nodes / networkpolicies 权限，见下）；容器 CPU 限流指标（本环境未配置 metrics 工具集）。因此 recs 那 1.5 s 的**具体机制仍属推测**。

---

## 建议修复

1. **立即**：对 `recommendationservice` 做一次 `kubectl rollout restart`（重建它被 13:18 那波 productcatalog 重启打坏的 gRPC/OTel 状态），这是当前唯一还在拖慢页面的组件。
2. **验证限流**：`recommendationservice` 上限只有 `cpu: 200m`（request 100m），Python + `opentelemetry-instrument` 很容易撞 CFS 配额。用 `kubectl top pod -n boutique` / `container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total` 确认；若确实限流，把 limit 提到 500m–1 并观察 `/product` 是否回到 ~0.3 s。同时确认 OTel span 导出指向的 collector 是否可达（同步导出超时同样会表现为"handler 已跑完但响应晚 1.5 s"）。
3. **别让 Redis 成为单点脆弱环节**：`redis-cart` 用 `emptyDir`（重启即丢购物车）+ `memory: 256Mi` limit（实际跑的是 redis-stack 全模块版，基线内存偏高，随时可能 OOMKilled）。建议换 PVC，并把 limit 提到 512Mi 以上。
4. **排查谁在动集群**：13:18:28 `kubectl rollout restart productcatalogservice`、13:19:51 `kubectl-patch productcatalogservice Service(ports)`、13:21:48 `kubectl-set checkoutservice`、13:21:57 `kubectl rollout restart redis-cart`、13:23:07 `kubectl-patch redis-cart Service(selector)` —— 这 5 次手工变更串起了整段故障窗口，建议复盘是否有自动化的"修复脚本"在反复重启业务 Pod。

> 权限提示：本次无法读取 `nodes`、`namespaces`、`networkpolicies`（`system:serviceaccount:diag-system:diag-agent` 无权限），如需排除节点压力/网络策略，请参考 https://holmesgpt.dev/data-sources/permissions/ 授权。

**日志说明**：以上日志均来自 `boutique` 命名空间各 Pod 的标准输出，默认窗口为最近 7 天中的最新条目，实际主要覆盖 **13:20–13:27**（另有一次 12:55 的对照查询）；单次最多展示 100 条并按 `filter` 过滤（例如前端按 `request complete` / `request error`，cartservice 按 `RedisConnectionException|ConnectTimeout|SocketClosed`），每处均标注了命中数与被省略条数。

You are HolmesGPT version dev-unknown, an AI agent for troubleshooting and answering questions about DevOps, IT and observability systems, using tool calls to gather data.
Make multiple independent tool calls in parallel whenever possible — it saves the user time.
Do not say 'based on the tool output' or explicitly refer to tools at all.
If, after answering, you realize more tool calls are needed, you may call more tools at that point.
If you have a concrete suggestion for how the user can fix something, share it even if not asked explicitly.



If you are unsure how to satisfy the user's request, gather more information — including by asking the user. Prefer finding the answer yourself when you can.









# Investigation guidelines

* Gather data with as many tool calls as needed before responding; keep going until you reach the deepest root cause you can find.
* Use the "five whys" approach: if a problem in service A traces to service B, investigate B too.
* Even after finding a root cause, keep investigating to find other possible causes and exact details (resource names, versions, labels). If there are multiple possible causes, list them in a numbered list.
* Always provide specific details from the user's environment — exact resource names, namespaces, versions — not generic examples.
* If you cannot find the resource the user referred to, assume a possible typo: try substrings and spelling variations.
* **Adjacent / similarly-named entities:** when the exact entity the user named has no data but similar-named ones do (siblings, same prefix/namespace), report both facts: state explicitly that you found nothing for the exact name (verbatim), report what you found in the similar entities, clearly labeled as coming from a different, related entity — never silently merge the user's name into the found ones — and suggest the user verify the name.
* Distinguish confirmed facts (directly observed in tool output) from hypotheses. Use hedging language ("possible", "likely", "may") for anything not directly confirmed; if the analysis is inconclusive, say so.
* Treat error messages as exact diagnostic evidence: `authentication failed` / `password authentication failed` for user X means user X EXISTS; `role does not exist` / `user not found` means the user is absent. These are mutually exclusive — never add "or the user may not exist" to an authentication failure.
* Do not conclude a resource is absent from a running system just because it isn't in deployment configuration — stateful systems accumulate state (SQL, API calls, admin operations) that leaves no K8s trace. If you can't read a value (e.g. a Secret), say you couldn't verify it rather than guessing.
* Data often contains errors that are irrelevant to the question — ignore them in your conclusion unless you tied them to the actual problem.
* ALWAYS check application logs when investigating whether an app, pod, service or deployment has issues — "running" and healthy-looking does not mean issue-free.

# Impact and blast radius

* Name an entity as affected only when you observed evidence for THAT entity — its own event, status/condition, log line or metric — and say what that evidence is (e.g. "`checkout-cache`: Evicted event, now Pending").
* Never widen the blast radius by inference. A node condition does not tell you which pods it hit; a failing dependency does not tell you which of its clients broke; an unhealthy shared component does not mean its consumers are unhealthy. Check each entity before you name it, or do not name it — sampling a workload's replicas characterizes the WORKLOAD, so attribute what you found to it rather than to replicas you did not look at.
* A restart, recreation, error or status change on an entity during the incident window is not impact until you have read its reason and found that it ties to this cause: the event's reason and message and who emitted it (`Evicted` from the kubelet is impact; `SuccessfulCreate` from a controller is a rollout), the container's last-state reason and exit code (`OOMKilled` vs `Completed`), or the log line. A pod that is 5 minutes old on a node that had trouble 5 minutes ago was not necessarily evicted — check what created it. Coincidence in time is not causation, and "also affected" is a claim that needs its own evidence.
* The same discipline applies to clearing entities: "X was unaffected" also needs a look. If you did not check, say you did not check.
* Entities you checked and found healthy are a finding worth reporting, not something to drop.
* Consequences you did not observe — downstream services, customer impact, data loss, other namespaces or clusters — are either verified before you state them, or marked explicitly as unverified with what would confirm them.
* Counts and scope words ("all", "several", "cluster-wide", "also affected") must match what you actually observed. Do not generalize from a sample you did not take.
* When you write up impact, sort every entity you name into one of four groups and label them: **Affected** — only entities with their own eviction, kill, error or failure evidence tied to this cause. Every line here quotes the exact reason token that proves it, in parentheses: `Evicted`, `OOMKilled`, `BackOff`, `Failed`, `Unhealthy` on a long-running pod, an error log line. If you cannot quote such a token for that entity, it does not go here — `SuccessfulDelete`, `SuccessfulCreate`, `Scheduled`, `Started` and a probe miss at startup are not among them. A recreation, restart or probe miss inside the window is never enough on its own, whatever sub-label you give it; **Checked, healthy** — you looked and found nothing wrong; **Changed during the window for another reason** — it restarted, was recreated or errored, and you name what did it (a controller rollout, a scheduled job, an operator, a probe at startup) and how you know; **Not checked**. Anything that changed during the window and that you cannot place in the first or third group goes in the fourth — it is not impact, and it does not go under an impact heading with a time-window qualifier as a substitute for a cause.

# If investigating Kubernetes problems

* Run as many kubectl commands as needed, walking the ownership chain (e.g. deployment → replicaset → pod) and checking both resource status and application logs.
* When a pod crashed or an application errors, always run kubectl_describe and fetch the logs.
* Don't stop at surface answers like "the pod is pending" or "node affinity doesn't match" — say why (which resource is short, which label doesn't match) and how to fix it.
* When many pods are affected, checking up to 3 representative pods per deployment is enough — to conclude about the DEPLOYMENT. Report the finding against the deployment; name an individual pod only when you looked at that pod.
* Eviction and OOM leave their mark on the pod: an `Evicted` event from the kubelet, or `OOMKilled` as a container's last termination reason. A pod that was deleted and recreated by its own controller — `SuccessfulDelete` / `SuccessfulCreate` from the daemonset-, replicaset- or statefulset-controller, a new pod name, a fresh `pod-template-generation`, Restart Count 0 — was rolled out or rescheduled by that controller, not damaged by the node, even when it happened in the same minute as the incident. For any pod younger than the incident, ask two things before you write about it: who created it (the `SuccessfulCreate` emitter), and whether the same controller replaced its siblings on other nodes in the same minutes — nodes that had no trouble. If it did, it was a rollout; write it as one, under "changed for another reason", never under impact. A startup readiness-probe miss on such a fresh pod is part of starting, not impact. Count a pod as affected only on its own eviction or kill evidence.
* If the user says something isn't working: describe the owner workload and pods (looking for transient issues), check for misconfigured ingresses/services, and read application logs for runtime issues.



# Available Toolsets
## Logs

* ALWAYS tell the user what logs you fetched and how: the time period covered (even if it was just the default, e.g. "Logs from last 1 hour..."), any limit applied and how many logs were shown vs total (e.g. "Showing last 100 lines"), and any filter used (e.g. "Logs filtered for 'error':").

* Use the tool `fetch_pod_logs` to access an application's logs yourself — do not ask users to do so.
* Before fetching logs, ensure the pod exists using kubectl tools. If you find no logs, double-check that the namespace and pod name are exact. If you weren't given the exact pod name or namespace (e.g. only an application or deployment name), find the right pods with kubectl tools and infer from there; ask the user only if you can't.
* If you have an issue/finding id, use `fetch_finding_by_id` for the issue's time information (`starts_at`, `updated_at`, `ends_at`); then use `start_time=-300` (5 minutes before `end_time`) and `end_time=<issue start_at time>`, widening or narrowing if you get too few or too many logs.
* If the user did not ask about a specific timeframe, omit `start_time` and `end_time` to use the default.

# Disabled & failed Toolsets

These toolsets are DISABLED (unconfigured) unless marked FAILED (misconfigured). Setup docs per toolset: `https://holmesgpt.dev/data-sources/builtin-toolsets/<name before any slash>/` unless a different URL is given.

# Handling Permission Errors

If a tool hits a permissions error (e.g. `Error from server (Forbidden):`): identify the missing resource, API group and verbs from the error; check which user/service account you run as and its permissions; report this to the user with a link to https://holmesgpt.dev/data-sources/permissions/



# Special cases

* Distinguish "I investigated and found error X caused this problem" from "errors prevented me from completing the investigation". A permission error when running a tool follows the Handling Permission Errors section; a permission error found *inside* a pod's logs is a root cause to explain to the user.
* Issues are a subset of findings. When asked about an issue or finding and you have an id, use `fetch_finding_by_id`.
* Reuse results of tools that were already called. If a tool call returns nothing, adjust the parameters instead of repeating it verbatim. When unsure which namespace a resource is in, use a cluster-level tool to locate it.



# Style guide

* Reply with terse output; be painfully concise; drop filler words.
* But never at the expense of important data like the root cause and how to fix it.
* Distinguish confirmed facts from hypotheses ("possible cause", "might be").

messages.reasoning_content:
The recommendationservice filter returns 0 due to the tool's multi-line log handling. Let me instead approach the timing question with a cleaner method: compare recs [Recv] log timestamps against the frontend's per-request timeline for a case where recs is the LAST call. The checkout page: frontend started 41.610, recs log 42.805, complete 44.366.

Hmm.

Alternative clean method: the frontend logs "request started" and then specific "serving product page"/"view user cart" lines, then complete. Not hop-level.

Let me think about what else could add 1.5s to recs.

Idea: check the productcatalogservice pod's TCP/CPU. Consider that the productcatalogservice pod was recreated at 13:18:28 → new IP 10.244.0.33. The recs gRPC channel resolved "productcatalogservice:3550" → ClusterIP. gRPC python uses the ClusterIP. kube-proxy DNAT per connection → new pod → works.

Hmm, BUT: does the recs channel maybe use the old productcatalog pod's *IP* (10.244.0.x) directly? gRPC resolves DNS to ClusterIP only, so no.

Let me check the productcatalog Service patch at 13:19:51 for f:ports — maybe today's targetPort was changed to something wrong then reverted? But current value 3550 → 3550 works.

Honestly, maybe I should look at this from the "what did the operator change" angle: multiple k8s objects were touched: productcatalog deployment (13:18:28 rollout), productcatalog service (13:19:51 ports patch), checkoutservice deployment (13:21:48 template set), redis deployment (13:21:57 rollout), redis service (13:23:07 selector patch). These are likely remediation attempts by whoever is on-call, or by an automated agent. This cluster appears to have "kubectl-set image" style changes.

Hold on — kubectl-set on checkoutservice template at 13:21:48, kubectl-rollout (which is what `kubectl rollout restart`? no, rollout restart sets annotation) — "kubectl-rollout" manager = `kubectl rollout restart`? Actually `kubectl rollout restart` uses the "kubectl-rollout" manager and patches spec.template.metadata.annotations → matches hasTemplate true. So:
- productcatalogservice: `kubectl rollout restart` at 13:18:28
- redis-cart: `kubectl rollout restart` at 13:21:57
- checkoutservice: `kubectl set ...` (kubectl-set) at 13:21:48

So someone restarted productcatalog and redis, and did `kubectl set` on checkout. These are manual interventions during the incident.

Interesting: the checkout pod at 13:21:48 (kubectl set image? or set env?) — but the pod is in the SAME RS 5d5f4589c5 created 12:30:32, and the pod's image equals the deployment. If `kubectl set` changed something in the template, a NEW RS would be created. The RS is old, so `kubectl set` must have set a value equal to the current one (e.g., `kubectl set image` with the same image → no template change... but managedFields says template owned). Hmm, maybe `kubectl set env` with the same value → no change → no new RS. But the pod was recreated at 13:21:48, which means the old pod was deleted — maybe by a restart of a non-existent rollout... 

Alternatively, the pod was OOMKilled/evicted and recreated by the RS. Wait — the checkout pod start 13:21:48 and container startedAt 13:21:48. Hmm, "restartCount 0". If a container restarts in-place, restartCount increments. So it's a new pod → old pod deleted. Deletion could be from eviction (node pressure) or manual `kubectl delete pod`.

Given all this, the cluster had a series of interventions that are consistent with an already-broken environment being "played with". My job is to explain the slowness.

Let me refocus: what could make ~1.5s delay after recs logs its line? If the log is at the END of the handler, the remaining 1.5s = network hop back + frontend finishing. The frontend go gRPC call to recs on same node should be <10ms.

UNLESS the frontend's recs call has retry/timeout... Hmm.

Hmm wait — maybe the [Recv] log IS at receipt, and ListProducts from recs takes 1.4s. Then what does productcatalog do that's slow for recs but not for frontend? 

AH WAIT. Maybe productcatalogservice is CPU-throttled but the frontend's home page request is FAST because... no, same server.

Hmm, unless the home page products are cached... In boutique v0.10.3, productcatalogservice has no cache. The frontend home page takes 0.3s with 1 ListProducts + ~10 currency conversions. So ListProducts ≈ 0.1s at most.

So recs' ListProducts should also be ~0.1s. Unless recs' gRPC channel is degraded and each call pays ~1.4s.

I think that's exactly it: recs' channel to productcatalogservice is broken/recovering. Evidence: we saw the UNAVAILABLE burst at 13:20:19-22 while productcatalog was down. Since the recs process is long-lived (started 12:30), its channel state after the outage could be persistently degraded... but gRPC recovers.

Hmm. Alternatively, if recs logs [Recv] at receipt and it calls ListProducts which gets UNAVAILABLE and raises... no, then errors would surface to the frontend ("failed to get recommendations"), and we saw no frontend errors after 13:23:08. Actually, wait: does the frontend tolerate recommendation errors? In boutique v0.10.3 productHandler:
```
recommendations, err := fe.getRecommendations(r.Context(), sessionID(r), p.Id, p.Categories)
if err != nil {
    renderHTTPError(log, r, w, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get product recommendations"), http.StatusInternalServerError)
    return
}
```
Not tolerated → 500. Loadgenerator showed failures earlier 14% cumulative; those may have stopped.

OK. Let me try yet another approach to pin the current 2.1s: use the frontend's own log lines with finer granularity. The frontend logs "serving product page" right after getting the product:

From the first fetch:
- 13:23:10.544 "serving product page" (product 6E92ZMYYFZ) → complete 13:23:10.553 (8ms!) Wait: "serving product page" at .544376 and "request complete" at .553064 = 8ms! That contradicts... Oh! That first one took only 8ms. So the timing varies hugely: one product page 8ms, others 2.1s.

Interesting! So the distribution is bimodal: some pages very fast (8ms), most ~2.1s. Hmm, but 8ms for a full product page? That's suspiciously fast — perhaps duplicate/mislabeled.

Let's re-read the first frontend log window (13:23:10-13:23:23):
- req b16b1564: request started 10.774 (product 1YMWWN1N4O), serving 10.774, complete 12.667 → 1893ms.
- req 3868703a: started 11.100, serving 11.100, complete 13.317 → 2217ms
- req 3e8f6411 (/): started 11.523, home 11.523, complete 11.813 → 289ms
- req a6ffbdaa: started 12.432, serving 12.432, complete 14.571 → 2138
- ...
The 8ms one: req 1818d97c: "serving product page" 13:23:10.544376 and complete 13:23:10.553064 → 8ms?? But took_ms=8. Hmm, that request must have started earlier (before the window). So product page served in 8ms — total 8ms from "serving product page" to complete. Hmm, that means the whole downstream chain took 8ms?! That is a request where everything was fast.

Wait, "serving product page" is logged after fetching product+currency+cart? Let me recall the handler:
```
p, err := fe.getProduct(...)
currencies, err := fe.getCurrencies(...)
price, err := fe.convertCurrency(...)
cart, err := fe.getCart(...)
recommendations, err := fe.getRecommendations(...)
ad := fe.chooseAd(...)
render template
```
And "serving product page" is logged right before rendering (after all the calls). So 8ms after "serving product page" to complete is normal for ANY request (the log is at the end).

Ah, that changes my analysis! The "serving product page" log line is near the END. So the 2.1s occurs BEFORE "serving product page".

So for req b16b1564: started 10.774 → serving 10.774 (same ms!?) → complete 12.667. Hmm, "request started" 10.774317 and "serving product page" 10.774382 — same millisecond. That can't include downstream calls...

Unless the log line "serving product page" is at the START of the handler. Let me check upstream code:

```go
func (fe *frontendServer) productHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	log := r.Context().Value(ctxKeyLog{}).(logrus.FieldLogger)
	id := mux.Vars(r)["id"]
	if id == "" {
		renderHTTPError(log, r, w, errors.New("product id not specified"), http.StatusBadRequest)
		return
	}
	log.WithField("id", id).WithField("currency", currentCurrency(r)).
		Debug("serving product page")

	p, err := fe.getProduct(r.Context(), id)
	...
```
Yes! "serving product page" is logged at the START of the handler. So the 2.1s is after that line — consistent with my earlier analysis (downstream calls take ~2s).

And the 8ms request: started-unknown, serving at 10.544, complete 10.553 → 8ms total. So SOME product page requests complete in 8ms! That means the downstream services CAN be fast. Hmm!! So the 2.1s isn't uniform for all requests.

But then in the last minute sample, nearly all product pages were ~2.1s. What about the faster ones? The distribution seems mostly 2.1s with occasional fast.

Bimodal: some requests ~8ms, most ~2.1s. Hmm, if the delay were a queue/lock, you'd see this.

What is bimodal 2.1s vs 8ms? A lock! Or a per-connection issue. Consider the frontend's gRPC client connections: Go gRPC client with DNS resolver; if a connection goes bad, requests wait.

Alternatively, the recommendationservice: Python gRPC ThreadPoolExecutor with N workers. Each request is fast (8ms), but... no.

Hmm, what about the cartservice? .NET with SE.Redis. GetCart when connection is DOWN: the RedisCache.GetAsync may block up to the 5s timeout... but errors stopped.

Wait, cart errors stopped at 13:23:08 but cartservice might still be failing internally — no, frontend would log "could not retrieve cart".

Hmm, alternatively the delay is the currencyservice (Node.js, single-threaded!) — but home page does 10 currency conversions in 0.3s.

Let me think about the bimodality: ~0.7s, 1.9s, 2.1s, 2.2s vs 8ms. Let me count: in the 13:25:28-45 window, product page took_ms: 2200, 2136, 2131, 2182, 2148, 2154, 2131, 2071, 2129, 2130, 2133, 2143, 2100 — ALL ~2.1s, no fast ones. In the 13:23:10-23 window: 8, 1893, 2217, 289(home), 2138, 2218, 316, 1792, 2095, 2081, 2164, 2109, 2140, 2204, 2127, 2018, 2143, 1794, 2072, 350(home), 2204, 2143.

So one 8ms outlier. And POST /cart = 293-322ms; POST /setCurrency 0ms; home 289-350ms.

So product/cart pages consistently ~2.1s. The 8ms outlier probably was a cached/error case.

OK so ~1.8s added to every page that calls recs (product, cart, checkout/order).

Now — is it recs or is it ads+shipping? cart page has no ads; product page has no shipping. Both slow. Cart page: getCart, products, convert, shipping quote, recs. 

What if the ~1.8s is in cartservice GetCart after all, and the 8ms/ 300ms cases are just... no: POST /cart (AddItem) 300ms is cartservice too, and GET /cart page includes getCart + more.

Hmm, hold on! What about the fact that cartservice is .NET and its Redis multiplexer is in a broken state? After the redis outage, SE.Redis's connection may be in a degraded state where each command waits for a reconnect cycle (~1.5s) but eventually succeeds. That would ADD ~1.5s to every GetCart/AddItem call... but AddItem is 300ms. Hmm, AddItem = 300ms consistently. So cartservice is healthy.

So GetCart ~300ms too, leaving recs as the only common slow call. And the delay of ~1.5-1.8s in recs.

Let me now try to measure recs' internal time using its OWN logs: if [Recv] is logged at handler start, then between the [Recv] log and the response there's the ListProducts call. I can test which by looking at log ordering relative to a burst: at 13:20:19-22, productcatalog was down. The recs exception traceback shows ListProducts raised. Does the [Recv] line appear BEFORE the traceback for those failed requests? If yes, [Recv] is at start. Let me check logs around 13:20:19 with filter "13:20" or get unfiltered logs in that window and see the sequence: [Recv] then traceback, or traceback only.

That's a concrete test! If in failed requests we see a [Recv] line followed by the exception, then [Recv] is logged at receipt (before ListProducts). If we see only tracebacks without [Recv], the log is at the end.

The tracebacks at 13:20:15-22 have created_time; the [Recv] lines shown are at 13:20:23.48-23.90 (epoch 1794748823 = 13:20:23). So the errors (13:20:15-22) do NOT have corresponding [Recv] lines → meaning [Recv] is logged AFTER ListProducts succeeds (i.e., at the end of the handler).

Wait: connection refused to the ClusterIP 10.96.32.253 means no endpoints → REJECT. So productcatalog SERVICE had no ready endpoints at 13:20:15-22! No — for a plain service, EndpointSlice includes the pod if ready (readiness is pod-level). Port mismatch wouldn't remove endpoints; it would route to a wrong port → connection refused SYN to podIP:wrongport.

Hmm, but the error message says ClusterIP:3550 "Connection refused" — the client connects to ClusterIP:3550. If the Service's targetPort were wrong, the connection would fail with refused (RST from pod). So the 13:19:51 ports patch could have broken routing! And then... it's now back to 3550→3550. But recs works now.

Hmm, but wait: the current slowness. If the productcatalog Service's targetPort is currently correct, recs' ListProducts would be fast.

But my timing analysis showed: page start +0.6s = [Recv] log time (i.e., after recs' ListProducts!). And the page completes 1.5s AFTER recs finished its work. Contradiction? Unless the [Recv] log is at 0.6s because ListProducts took ~0.5s (not 0.6s of frontend pre-work).

But the /cart page has recs last... let's check: cart page 8bca04e5 started 13:25:31.651, completed 13:25:33.819 (2168ms). [Recv] candidates: 13:25:31.931 (+0.28s) or 13:25:33.473 (+1.82s).

```go
func (fe *frontendServer) viewCartHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {

```
